evidence: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:32-34 approves durable transcript requests, concurrent dispatch, coverage/output references and resumed work, then explicitly leaves out-of-order results open. DESIGN-NOTES.md:248,256-259 confirms the main occupant need not wait, completion includes transcript identity, processed-through position and summary path, and no ordering rule is settled. Full-text search of all four artifacts for summary/result/coverage/recovery and equivalent handling found no monotonic current-result selection, artifact versioning, or overwrite rule. Thus an implementation that treats the last completion as current could expose a shorter older summary after a newer one, undermining replacement-occupant recovery (HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:37,139). Narrowing: neither a single summary pointer nor shared-path overwrite is specified, so regression is a plausible failure mode of the acknowledged contract gap, not an established behavior or actual data loss. Significant continuity risk, but draft design claims no implementation readiness (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:58).
